<explanation>
To capture ClassroomIO.com’s architecture in a system-design diagram, follow these steps tailored to this monorepo’s structure:

1. Identify the Main Components  
   - Frontends (all in SvelteKit/Next.js):  
     • Landing site (`apps/classroomio-com`)  
     • Dashboard LMS (`apps/dashboard`)  
     • Documentation site (`apps/docs`)  
   - Backend microservice (`apps/backend`)  
   - Database & Auth (Supabase project under `supabase/`)  
   - Serverless functions (Supabase Edge Functions and SvelteKit API routes)  
   - Shared libraries and tooling (`packages/*`, `shared`, `tsconfig`, `_template`)  
   - External integrations: OpenAI, PostHog, Sentry, Cal.com, Lemonsqueezy, Polar, email provider, Inbucket  

2. Determine Relationships & Data Flows  
   - End-users (students, teachers, admins) open either the landing site or the dashboard in their browser.  
   - The landing site handles marketing pages, blog CMS (static MDX + SvelteKit), and simple form submissions via SvelteKit API routes to Supabase or the backend.  
   - The dashboard app is the primary SPA/SSR LMS. It authenticates via Supabase Auth, reads/writes data over the Supabase REST/GraphQL API, and invokes serverless functions for AI content generation, grading, notifications, etc.  
   - The backend microservice (Node.js + Puppeteer utilities, video upload, PDF certificate generation, email dispatch) runs as a standalone Docker service. Dashboard and Supabase Edge Functions call it over HTTP when heavy‐duty processing is needed.  
   - Supabase Edge Functions (in `supabase/functions/`) handle lightweight serverless endpoints (e.g., webhooks, custom grading triggers).  
   - All persistent data (users, courses, lessons, assignments, community Q&A) lives in the Supabase PostgreSQL instance, with RLS policies. Supabase Storage holds uploaded videos and course assets.  
   - External billing services (Lemonsqueezy, Polar) are called by serverless functions and backend routes.  
   - Analytics events are sent from both frontends to PostHog, with errors reported to Sentry.  

3. Highlight Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Monorepo microfrontends and microservices: each major “app” folder is its own deployment unit, sharing typed contracts via the `shared`/`packages` libraries.  
   - SSR with SvelteKit and Next.js for SEO and fast first load; API routes co-locate backend logic when simple.  
   - Serverless tier (Supabase Edge Functions) for low-latency logic close to the database.  
   - Dedicated backend service for CPU‐intensive tasks (video, PDF, Puppeteer).  
   - Clear separation of concerns: UI layer ──> API layer ──> database/storage layer.  

4. Diagram Elements & Notation Guidelines  
   - Use distinct shapes:  
     • Rectangle for frontends and backend service  
     • Cylinder for relational database  
     • Bucket icon for object storage  
     • Cloud icons for third-party services  
     • Serverless icon (lightning bolt) for Supabase Functions  
   - Color-code by layer:  
     • Blue: UI (landing, dashboard, docs)  
     • Green: backend service & functions  
     • Orange: database & storage  
     • Purple: external integrations  
   - Draw directional arrows for request/response:  
     • From “User Browser” to each frontend over HTTPS  
     • Frontend → Supabase Auth/API/Functions  
     • Frontend & Functions → Backend service (when needed)  
     • Backend & Functions → Supabase Storage & PostgreSQL  
     • Functions → External services (OpenAI, billing, analytics, email)  
   - Label each arrow with the protocol or SDK used (e.g., REST, GraphQL, Supabase JS SDK, HTTP POST).  
   - Group related components in bounded “deployment” boxes (e.g., “Monorepo → CI/CD → GitHub Actions” on one side).  

5. Tailoring to this Full-Stack LMS  
   - Emphasize user flows:  
     • Marketing visitor → contact form → SvelteKit API → Supabase  
     • Student login → Dashboard → Supabase Auth → read/write course data → Supabase Functions for AI  
     • Teacher adds lesson → Dashboard → Supabase → triggers video processing in backend → stores in Supabase Storage  
   - Show how self-hosting works with Docker Compose: local Supabase, backend container, dashboard & landing served via Vite.  
   - Call out the package generator CLI (`packages/course-app`) as a developer‐tool component.  

6. Final Checklist for the Diagram  
   - Clear component labels (e.g., “Dashboard App (SvelteKit)”)  
   - Directional arrows with protocols  
   - Color or shape differentiation by layer  
   - Grouping for deployment units (Docker vs. Supabase vs. Vercel)  
   - Legend that explains colors/shapes  

By following these guidelines, you will end up with a detailed, accurate depiction of ClassroomIO’s architecture—covering the separation of frontend, API, backend‐processing service, database, storage, serverless functions, and external dependencies.
